newsitem.title: GREECE: BUY GREEK STOCKS AFTER DUST SETTLES - ING BARINGS.
newsitem.headline: BUY GREEK STOCKS AFTER DUST SETTLES - ING BARINGS.

text.p: Greek equities may be a buying opportunity after Thursday's scandal-related 3.31 percent plunge but investors should let the dust settle before taking action, said ING Barings.

"We recommend letting the dust settle before taking any action. The risk of another market interruption has subsided, but not disappeared," said an ING Barings in its "Should you react to the crisis?" report.
The recent crisis did not change the country's fundamentals. Although improving, there was need of hard evidence that reforms are being implemented.
"The Athens bourse crisis highlighted flaws in the stock market administration but it all started when the government started dealing with precisely these flaws," it said.

In its view the crisis was a teething problem with the government slow to react at first. It eventually reacted appropriately by injecting liquidity and legislating measures to to restore short-term confidence in the system, it said.

"However, the solution was inadequate. The government did not create an automatic mechanism which will provide liquidity and guarantee settlement of past transactions when and if another local broker fails," analyst Yiannis Protopapadakis said.
Based on a limited poll of 10 brokers and fund managers the market expected another 5.0 percent fall stabilising at a median 835 points on the benchmark index. The answers ranged from 750 to 880.
But the stock market rebounded on Friday cutting Thursday's losses and settling 1.37 percent higher at 890.39 on moderate turnover of 6.06 billion drachmas.
ING Barings liked shares of Hellenic Bottling , OTE telecom, Delta Dairy, Michaniki, AEGEK and Silver & Baryte .

"What you see is not what you get. Prices on your screen are not representative of the price you would get on a sizeable trade. Much of Thursday's trading activity was triggered by liquidity constraints of small local brokers," it said.
"Their liquidity has been stretched to unprecedented levels and the market's overall volume is too low for reliable pricing." --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
